audit.why: 49.2% over 1256 games at 7/10 TRICKY fits the range gap: Arcanopulse 750, Eye of Destruction 1000, Shocking Orb 1050 against Annie's 625 Q. She cannot contest until Tibbers exists.

audit.whatIsWrong: All seven phases[].side read 'Skill' while win[] read Xerath/Xerath/Xerath/Xerath/Annie/Annie/Annie.
audit.why: Every row disagreed between the two layers. win[] matches packet.levelChart and matches the content whys, which describe Xerath dominating until 6 and Annie flipping it. 'Skill' across the board also contradicts the 7/10 difficulty.
audit.corrected: All seven phases[].side realigned to the win[] chart as one atomic group.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing anywhere stated that Rite of the Arcane is a channel Annie can cancel — the single most important interaction in the matchup.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'Xerath immobilizes himself and gains numerous long-range barrages', flagged channel/interruptible. A stocked Pyromania stun or a Tibbers cast lands on a Xerath who is rooted in place and stops the ultimate outright. Xerath's ult is 130/115/100s — the same cooldown as Tibbers — so cancelling it is a full-cooldown trade in Annie's favour.
audit.corrected: Added to breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[2].d and spikes[1].text.

audit.whatIsWrong: packet.defects flagged that no cooldown-sequencing advice existed anywhere in this matchup. Shocking Orb was called 'matchup-defining' with no number.
audit.why: Shocking Orb is 13/12.5/12/11.5/11s and is his only CC; Arcanopulse is 9/8/7/6/5s. Those two numbers are the entire step-up schedule.
audit.corrected: Concrete 13s and 9s rank-1 numbers written into breakdown.cooldowns and dosFull[0].d.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.wave used the generic 'every assassin timer in the game' template.
audit.why: Xerath is not an assassin and does not punish a shoved wave by diving — he punishes it by holding you off the crash at 1000+ range.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.carry and dontsFull[0].d were both name-swap templates.
audit.why: Against Xerath specifically, Annie's carry pattern is cancelling the ultimate and punishing a 13s Shocking Orb, not a generic radius.

edits.before: - Xerath Shocking Orb (Stun): matchup-defining — His only CC — dodge the orb and his artillery never converts into a kill. Count it out loud if you must. - Your E Molten Shield has one job: the moment it all goes wrong. - The R has one too: the moment it all goes right.
edits.after: - Xerath Shocking Orb: 13s at rank 1 — his only CC, so step up on its downtime and the artillery never converts. Arcanopulse is 9s. - Rite of the Arcane roots him while he channels: a stocked stun or Tibbers cancels it outright, so hold the glow when he ults.

edits.before: His only CC — dodge the orb and his artillery never converts into a kill. Commit on its cooldown, never into it.
edits.after: Shocking Orb is 13s at rank 1 and his only CC — dodge the orb and step in during those thirteen seconds.

edits.before: Xerath spends Shocking Orb (Stun) early — the closest thing this matchup has to a guarantee.
edits.after: Xerath channels Rite of the Arcane — a stocked stun cancels it and ends him mid-barrage.

edits.before: That’s Xerath’s bread-and-butter play — deny it and they run out of answers.
edits.after: His Arcanopulse outranges your Q by 125 — that is a poke war you cannot answer.

edits.before: Carry through the one button — Flash-Tibbers on two is a won fight; your whole game is engineering the radius.
edits.after: Carry by cancelling him — a stun landed mid-Rite of the Arcane trades your button for his 100-second one.

edits.before: Best wave: a Q-refund farmed wave you never push past river — your kill threat is Flash radius, not wave state. Worst wave: a shoved wave with zero stacks and Tibbers down — every assassin timer in the game points at that picture. Crash timing: every crash should buy something — a reset, a plate, a roam. Autopilot shoving buys ganks.
edits.after: Best wave: a Q-refund farmed wave you never push past river — your kill threat is Flash radius, not wave state. Worst wave: a shoved wave with zero stacks and Tibbers down — Xerath holds you off the crash from 1000 range and takes the whole thing free. Crash timing: every crash should buy something — a reset, a plate, a roam. Autopilot shoving buys ganks.

edits.before: Rite of the Arcane still lets him poke you from another zip code, but Tibbers finally gives you a gap-closing threat that forces him to respect your all-in near turret range.
edits.after: Rite of the Arcane still hits you from another zip code, but it roots him in place while he channels — a stocked stun or a Tibbers cast cancels it outright and ends the barrage early.

edits.before: Tibbers at level 6 finally gives Annie a real engage threat, flipping the matchup in her favor
edits.after: Tibbers flips it at 6: it both engages and cancels the Rite of the Arcane channel outright

edits.before: Look for jungle ganks to help you close the gap onto him since solo engage is very hard
edits.after: Punish his ultimate — the channel roots him, so a stun there is a free kill window

notes: All seven level-chart rows disagreed between layers here (phases all 'Skill' vs win[] Xerath x4 then Annie x3); proposed as one atomic group toward the packet chart.
